title: Slender bar with hinged ends: critical load

source.work: ANSYS, Inc., Mechanical APDL Verification Manual (public help site ansyshelp.ansys.com)
source.location: VM127, 'Buckling of a Bar with Hinged Ends (Line Elements)' (https://ansyshelp.ansys.com/public/Views/Secured/corp/v252/en/ans_vm/Hlp_V_VM127.html)
source.notes: problem statement taken from the vendor page (text; the sketch was not readable). The page cites: Timoshenko, Strength of Materials, Part II, 3rd ed. 1956, p. 148, article 29 - NOT opened for this project; no number is taken from it. The page's 'Target' values are recorded as printed; the program's own results are not used.

analysis: Plane problem in the global X-Y plane (Y vertical); the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held; in-plane bending about local z. Bar of 200 in with hinged ends (the far end free to move axially), square section 0.5 in x 0.5 in (A = 0.25 in^2, I = 0.0052083 in^4), E = 30e6 psi; reference load 1 lb, so the buckling factor is the critical load in lb. Linear buckling analysis of the whole bar (the page models half of it by symmetry); the engine's member carries the exact stability functions. Iy = 1000 Iz so that the in-plane mode is the lowest (the square section has no preferred plane; the page's problem is plane). Reference values: computed here from this statement (verification/derive/vendor_reference.py); the textbook cited by the vendor page was not opened and no number is taken from it.

targets.precisionNote: evaluated here in double precision (smallest root of the characteristic equation sin(kL) = 0, P = k^2 EI); tolerance = policy floor 1e-6
printed "38.553"; tolerance = half a unit in the last printed digit
